title: Repayment Plans and Reduced Monthly Withholding — Benefit Debts and Overpayment Recovery Terms
content:
**Two arrangements.** A debtor with a debt in **Benefit Debts and Overpayment Recovery** may ask to repay in monthly installments paid directly, or to have the monthly withholding from benefit payments reduced. A repayment plan request is taken only on a debt whose status is active; the status is read from the debt record.

**Plan length.** A plan of up to the longest plan approved without a Financial Status Report for the debt type is approved on request. A plan longer than the longest plan approved with a Financial Status Report is not available.

> *Retired clause, no longer in force:* the former clause that a plan of up to the longest plan approved with a Financial Status Report is approved only with a Financial Status Report. It is retired and is not a basis for deciding a plan's length.

> *Retired clause, no longer in force:* the former clause that the installment must be at least the smallest plan installment and at least the balance divided by the plan's number of months, rounded up to the cent. It is retired and is not a basis for figuring an installment.

**Reduced withholding.** Reduced withholding is approved only with a Financial Status Report and never below the debt type's smallest reduced withholding.

**Due date and default.** The first installment is due the debt type's first-installment period, in calendar days, after approval. The plan is cancelled when the debt type's default count of consecutive installments is missed, after which full offset resumes. Consecutive missed installments are counted over the plan months from the plan's first month through the month before the current month: they are the most recent plan months, in an unbroken run, for which no direct payment for that plan month was received.

**Early payoff.** A debtor may pay off the balance early at any time without penalty. Direct payments may be made through the debt type's direct payment channels.

### Counting misses — hypothetical illustration

A plan whose first month is January, reviewed in May (plan months January to April counted):

| Plan month | Direct payment for that month |
|---|---|
| January | Received |
| February | Received |
| March | None |
| April | None |

The unbroken run of most recent months without a payment is March and April: two consecutive missed installments. Had a payment for April been received, the run would be zero, whatever happened in March.
